summary: Layers one CHOP's channels over another over a defined interval, with base hold, channel matching, easing, and rotation-aware blending options.
key_concepts: Layers the second input over the first input, with the first input as the base and the second input as the layer.
Designed for static multi-frame motion channels; the official docs direct time-sliced or single-frame blending to Blend CHOP instead.
Layer contribution is eased in and out across Start, Peak, Release, and End, and the base is unaffected outside the layer interval.
Base Hold 0 replaces the base when Effect is 1, while Base Hold 1 adds the layer to the base.
A connected third input overrides the Effect page using its first channel over the layer range.
Quaternion Blend and Shortest Path Rotation Blending handle rotation channels specially when quaternion attributes or rotation scopes are configured.

key_params.name: base
key_params.note: How much base input remains when the layer is fully active

key_params.name: match
key_params.note: Match channels by index, name, or channel union

key_params.name: quatrot
key_params.note: Use quaternion rotation blending when channels have quaternion attributes

key_params.name: rotscope
key_params.note: Rotation channels affected by special rotation blending

key_params.name: cyclelen
key_params.note: Cycle length for wraparound rotation blending

key_params.name: effect
key_params.note: Blend contribution when no third input overrides it

common_gotchas: Composite CHOP is intended for static multi-frame motion channels; use Blend CHOP for time-sliced or single-frame blends.
If a third input is connected, its first channel overrides the Effect page.
Base Hold 0 replaces the base when effect is 1; Base Hold 1 adds the layer to the base.
Channel matching by index is fragile when source channel order changes; prefer name matching when possible.
Quaternion blending expects quaternion attributes from Attribute CHOP.
